trello.name: Build frontend checkout with Stripe Elements and update pricing page
trello.desc: Owner: Jordan. Implement the checkout process using Stripe Elements, ensuring the checkout form matches the app's design and handles errors gracefully (invalid card details, insufficient funds). Update the pricing page to reflect the three subscription tiers: Basic ($29/month with basic AI model selection tool and limited features), Pro ($49/month with additional features and priority support), and Enterprise ($99/month with all features, custom support, and integration options). The design should be clean and straightforward with a clear feature comparison for each tier, a prominent checkout button, and a tooltip or help icon explaining what happens if a user chooses a different plan later. Deadline: within two weeks.

trello.name: Build user dashboard for subscription management
trello.desc: Owner: Jordan. Build the user dashboard to display current plan details and billing info, provide options to upgrade, downgrade, or cancel subscriptions, give access to invoices and payment history, and allow updating payment methods. The dashboard must be intuitive, reflect current subscription status in real-time, and notify users of changes such as successful plan upgrades or payment failures. Integrate the frontend with the backend API so subscription changes are reflected in real-time. Handle errors during integration and provide clear user notifications for events like subscription confirmations and payment errors, including instructions on how to fix failed payments. Deadline: within two weeks.

trello.name: Integrate Stripe API on backend and set up webhook handlers
trello.desc: Owner: Taylor. Integrate Stripe's API to handle all subscription-related backend tasks: creating subscriptions when a user selects a plan and completes payment, processing successful and failed payments, and managing webhooks. Set up webhook handlers for the following events: invoice.payment_succeeded (confirm successful payments and activate/continue subscription), invoice.payment_failed (notify users of failed payments, prompt them to update payment info, and send an email notification), and customer.subscription.deleted (update access rights and offer re-subscription). Ensure webhook handlers update the system correctly. Create test scenarios to simulate different events like payment failures and cancellations. Deadline: within two weeks.

trello.name: Prepare and share detailed test plan for subscription flow
trello.desc: Owner: Taylor. Prepare a detailed test plan and share it with Alex and Jordan. The plan should cover both manual and automated tests, including testing the entire subscription flow from sign-up to billing to managing the subscription. Test scenarios should simulate different events such as payment failures and cancellations. Ensure all edge cases are covered during the testing phase. Testing phase: one week after the initial integration is complete (approximately three weeks from now).

trello.name: Document API endpoints and webhook event handlers
trello.desc: Owner: Taylor. Document the API endpoints and webhook event handlers to make future maintenance and troubleshooting easier. This includes documenting how subscriptions are created, payments are processed, and webhook events (invoice.payment_succeeded, invoice.payment_failed, customer.subscription.deleted) are handled.

trello.name: Create help section and FAQ for subscription management
trello.desc: Owner: Jordan. Create a help section or FAQ that covers common issues and questions about subscriptions, including how users can manage their subscriptions, access invoices, and handle any issues. This should be available once the integration is live.

trello.name: Schedule follow-up meeting for next week
trello.desc: Owner: Alex. Set up a follow-up meeting for next week to review progress on the Stripe subscription integration and address any issues or blockers that have come up. Team members should reach out if they encounter blockers before the meeting.
